aiSettings.ruleHelp: As long as none of a user's roles has a quota stored, usage is unlimited. Once at least one role is configured, the highest value wins; an explicitly unlimited role wins over limited roles. 0 disables that quota. “Max memory entries per scope” is the exception: there “Unlimited” does not win but contributes nothing at all — the system limit applies only when none of the user's roles carries a number.

confirm.propose_server_lifecycle: The “{{operation}}” action affects server operation. Permissions and server state are checked again immediately before execution.
confirm.propose_backup: Create a server backup now? Permissions and server state are checked again immediately before execution.
confirm.propose_config_patch: Replace only the displayed passages in “{{path}}”? The rest of the file stays untouched. The change is stored permanently and rewritten before every start. Execution is blocked if the file changed in the meantime.
confirm.propose_config_set: Set the displayed settings in “{{path}}”? They are also stored permanently and rewritten before every start — even if the game rewrites its own configuration. Takes effect on the next restart.
confirm.propose_config_update: Write the displayed, revision-bound change to “{{path}}”? Execution is blocked if the file changed in the meantime.
confirm.propose_mod_install: Install the mod “{{path}}” through the existing installation path? The download runs in the background and the mod only takes effect after a restart.
confirm.propose_mod_toggle: Flip the switch for the mod “{{path}}”? No files are downloaded or deleted; it takes effect with the next start of the server.
confirm.propose_server_create: Create a new server? Blueprint, capacity, ports and permissions are checked exactly as they are when creating one through the panel.
confirm.propose_server_delete: Delete this server for good? Container, game files and database entry are removed. This cannot be undone — existing backups are the only source afterwards.
confirm.propose_backup_restore: Restore the backup “{{path}}”? The current state of the game files is overwritten. Everything since that backup is gone afterwards.
confirm.propose_bind_ip_update: Change the bind IP of this server? The server is restarted for it, and players have to connect through the new address.
confirm.propose_blueprint_change: Derive a new blueprint from this server? The blueprint is then available to everyone who may create servers.
confirm.propose_blueprint_delete: Permanently delete this unused community blueprint? It will no longer be available for new servers. Active servers using it prevent deletion.
confirm.propose_ai_tarif_role: Create the role “{{path}}”? It deliberately gets no permissions, only the AI quota shown — permissions are still granted through role management.
confirm.propose_hoster_integration: Save the shop integration “{{path}}”? Creating one also generates an API key that is shown exactly once and can only be rotated afterwards.
confirm.propose_hoster_product: Save the product mapping “{{path}}”? Every future purchase of this product creates a server with these limits — and, if configured, with the role shown.
confirm.propose_server_blueprint_switch: Switch this server to another blueprint? Start command, image and variables are replaced; the game files stay and may no longer match.
confirm.propose_guardian_tuning: Change the autopilot settings for this server? They apply to this server only and override what the blueprint specifies — the startup grace period, for instance, or the number of recovery attempts. The blueprint itself and every other server stay untouched; the autopilot tab then shows what applies, with a button to reset it.
confirm.propose_server_repair: Run the “{{operation}}” repair on this server's infrastructure? “repair_permissions” resets ownership of the server directory, “reallocate_port” reassigns occupied ports and restarts the server for it. Neither touches game files.
confirm.propose_file_delete: Delete the file “{{path}}”? Afterwards it can only be recovered from a backup. A snapshot is written to the file history before deleting.
confirm.propose_task_set: This task will run on its own from now on, even when you are not in the panel. It acts with your permissions and from your AI quota. You can pause or delete it any time from the chat.
confirm.propose_task_delete: This task will be removed for good and will no longer run. If it should only rest for a while, have it paused instead.
confirm.propose_restart_schedule_set: Configure this server's auto-restart like this? The schedule then appears in the server's restart section and stays editable by hand. If you later change it manually, AI management ends and the responsible task is paused.
confirm.propose_backup_schedule_set: Configure this server's auto-backup like this? The settings then appear in the server's backup section and stay editable by hand. If you later change them manually, AI management ends and the responsible task is paused.

autonomy.title: Autonomous mode
autonomy.descriptionPanel: Without a grant the AI asks before every action. With a panel-wide grant it executes permitted actions on all of your servers immediately.
autonomy.descriptionServer: Without a grant the AI asks before every action. With a grant it executes permitted actions on this server immediately.
autonomy.budgetHint: Executed automatically in the last hour: {{used}}. Once the budget is used up the AI asks again — nothing fails.
autonomy.boundary: Autonomous mode removes your confirmation and lets the Guardian engine wake the AI on a fault. Permissions, server locks and audit still apply unchanged — the AI cannot do anything you could not do yourself. Not included: deleting a server, wipe, reinstall, switching blueprints and backup restore. Those always require confirmation. When the AI hits such a step in the background, it emails you an approval link instead of giving up.
autonomy.confirmPanel:
The AI will then run permitted actions on all your servers without asking — including configuration changes, mod installs and creating new servers.

New: this also lets the Guardian engine wake the AI while you are away. When it reports a fault, the AI investigates on its own, takes a provably successful backup before touching any file, and tries to get the server running again — restart, directory permissions, port assignment, configuration, autopilot settings, and if needed deleting a broken file. It stays on it until the system reports the server healthy again. You then receive an email with the result.

Your permissions remain the boundary. It acts in your name and on your AI quota. Deleting a server, wipe, reinstall, switching blueprints and restoring a backup still always require your confirmation — in the background the AI asks for it by email and waits for your answer.
autonomy.confirmServer:
The AI will then run permitted actions on this server without asking — including configuration changes and mod installs.

New: this also lets the Guardian engine wake the AI while you are away. When it reports a fault on this server, the AI investigates on its own, takes a provably successful backup before touching any file, and tries to get it running again. You then receive an email with the result.

Your permissions remain the boundary. It acts in your name and on your AI quota. Delete, wipe, reinstall and restoring a backup still always require your confirmation.

Guardian faults will then only be reported, not fixed. The AI mentions them in your next chat and proposes something; it will only act once you confirm. If a server goes down at night, it stays down until someone looks.

intro.body:
A blueprint is a pure JSON definition for a server type—e.g., 'DayZ Server' or 'Minecraft Server', not the running server itself. It tells the panel which Docker image to use, what ports are needed, how to start, and where to get the server files (Steam, HTTPS, Image, or manual). Countless server instances can be created from a single blueprint.

Blueprints never contain scripts or hooks. They are strictly validated by the panel before execution, keeping the system fast and secure.

guardian.body: Guardian is an optional, strictly bounded agent capability. One switch in the web editor removes every Guardian block; when enabled, the editor offers only values supported by both backend and agent.
guardian.probesBody: Supported probes are process, TCP/UDP port, and the tcp, http-ping, minecraft-status, minecraft-query, and source-query application probes. Custom driver types cannot be configured.
guardian.parsersBody: Available parsers are linux-oom, java-stacktrace, nodejs-stacktrace, port-conflict, missing-runtime, corrupted-config, and startup-pattern.
guardian.actionsBody: Policies may trigger only restart, graceful_restart, clear_declared_lock_files, or quarantine. Lock files require a pre-approved safe relative path and reason.
guardian.matchesBody: The editor offers only exact failure IDs actually emitted by agent probes and parsers. Free-text matches are rejected.
guardian.operationBody: Attempt windows, cooldown, and success verification bound autonomous actions. Before clear_declared_lock_files, the agent backs up only explicitly declared lock files up to 1 MiB. protected_paths are exclusion boundaries and are not backed up. A quarantine release remains pending until the agent confirms a new observed state.

reference.body: All fields are strictly validated against the backend Pydantic schema upon upload.
reference.metaId: Unique technical ID. Uppercase letters and spaces are normalized to lowercase letters and underscores when saved. Cannot collide with native blueprints.
reference.metaDescription: Short description for the UI dropdown.
reference.runtimeEnv: Environment variables as a key-value dict. Values may contain port placeholders: {GAME_PORT}, {QUERY_PORT}, {RCON_PORT}, {VOICE_PORT}, {WEB_PORT}. {INSTALL_DIR} and {ENV.<KEY>} are NOT allowed in env values.
reference.runtimeStartup: Startup command (passed as argv, NO shell). Valid placeholders: {SERVER_NAME}, {GAME_PORT}, {QUERY_PORT}, {RCON_PORT}, {VOICE_PORT}, {WEB_PORT}, {INSTALL_DIR}, {MOD_ARG}. {SERVER_NAME} uses the individual MSM server name. Also {ENV.<KEY>} for custom env variables. Forbidden characters: $, backtick.
reference.runtimeEnsureDirs: Relative directories created inside the server directory before each start. Useful for profile, log, cache, or runtime folders expected by startup arguments.
reference.runtimeConfigPatches: List of configuration patches applied before start. Each patch requires: type, file, and value (plus section/key for 'ini' or regex for 'regex'). They apply to every server using this blueprint. Values for a single server are set by the AI via “Set a setting permanently” — those run after the blueprint patches and therefore override them.
reference.runtimeEnableExec: Enable the Exec tab. Default: false. Self-hosted, but commands run ONLY inside the MSM-managed container of this server, NEVER on the host or in other containers.
reference.runtimeExecTimeoutSeconds: Timeout per exec call in seconds (1..600). Default: 60.
reference.logsSources: Log sources for Guardian and the visible server console. stdout shows Docker output; safe relative file paths and simple filename wildcards are additionally followed live.
reference.logsRedact: Redactors applied to every displayed log source. Supports built-in types and safe regex: patterns; known secret assignments are always masked.
reference.logsMaxTailBytes: Maximum file-log data read per pass (1,024 to 1,048,576 bytes).
reference.configPatchType: Patch type. Valid values: ini, regex.
reference.configPatchFile: Relative file path, e.g. Config/Server.ini. No absolute paths and no '..'.
reference.configPatchRegex: Search pattern as a regular expression (required when type=regex).
reference.configPatchValue: Value. Allowed port placeholders: {GAME_PORT}, {QUERY_PORT}, {RCON_PORT}, {VOICE_PORT}, {WEB_PORT}. Not allowed: {ENV.<KEY>}, {MOD_ARG}, {INSTALL_DIR}.
reference.portsDesc: Declare the required port roles. The user assigns concrete numbers during creation. The same standard role may appear once per protocol, e.g. query/udp and query/tcp; MSM stores these as unique roles such as query and query_2.
reference.portsName: Port role. Do not write 'ports.name' as the value; use game, query, rcon, voice, web, or custom. Concrete port numbers are assigned later when creating the server.
reference.portsProtocol: tcp or udp. The protocol controls Docker mapping and firewall rules and can be changed later in the network panel.
reference.sourceType: Where server files come from: steam = SteamCMD, http = HTTPS archive, github = repository, dockerOnly = image contains everything, custom = custom runtime logic, manualUpload = user uploads files manually.
reference.sourceUpdateStrategy: Controls server file updates before start/restart: alwaysValidate = always run SteamCMD/install; checkBased = only when the update check reports an update (Steam: buildid compare); none = no auto-update.
reference.sourceSteam: Steam dedicated server: appId, platform, compatibility, requiresLogin, validate, optional branch (depot branch, default public).
reference.steamBranch: Optional. Steam depot branch for install and update check (e.g. conan-exiles-legacy). Omit for public. Workshop mods still use mods.workshopAppId.
reference.steamValidate: true (default): SteamCMD +app_update … validate. false: faster update without validate (e.g. large Proton/Wine apps).
reference.steamRequiresLogin: true when the global Steam account in panel settings is required for this app.
reference.sourceHttp: HTTPS URL to the server archive (zip/tar).
reference.sourceGithub: GitHub repo owner/repo, branch, optional subPath and setupCommands (argv). Private repos: PAT in Settings → GitHub, or MSM_GITHUB_CLONE_TOKEN on the host.
reference.sourceManual: List of required files if users must upload them manually.
reference.githubPrivateBody: For private repos, set a GitHub Personal Access Token in Settings → GitHub. Public repos work without a token.
reference.modsSupportsMods: Enables the Mod Manager tab for this server.
reference.modsSupportsCurseForge: Enables CurseForge integration for this server.
reference.modsCurseforgeGameId: Official CurseForge Game ID (e.g., 83374 for ARK: Survival Ascended, 432 for Minecraft).
reference.modsCurseforgeClassId: Optional. Filters for a CurseForge Category/Class ID (e.g., 6 for Minecraft Mods, 4552 for Bukkit/Paper Plugins).
reference.modsCurseforgeInstallPath: Optional. Relative target directory for downloaded mod files (e.g., mods or plugins).
reference.modsModStartupArgumentSeparator: Optional (Default: ';'). Separator between mod IDs in the startup argument (e.g., ',' for ARK: Survival Ascended).
reference.modsWorkshopAppId: Steam App ID of the workshop (e.g., 440900 for Conan Exiles).
reference.modsFilterTags: List of tags used to filter workshop mod search (e.g. ["Enhanced"]). Max. 10 tags (alphanumeric, spaces, _ , - , +).
reference.modsModStartupArgumentFormat: Format of the startup mod argument (e.g., -mod={mods};).
reference.modsModListFilePath: File path of the mod list file (e.g., ConanSandbox/Mods/modlist.txt).
reference.modsModListContent: Format of entries written to the mod list file (workshopIds, postInstallTargetBasenames).
reference.modsPostInstall: List of file operations run after mod downloads complete.
reference.backupIncludePaths: Optional. Relative paths/globs under install_dir for backups (config, saves, DB). Without a backup block: full server directory. Restore overwrites only these paths.
reference.runtimeUser: Numeric User:Group in container (e.g. 1000:1000). Must not be root (0).
reference.runtimeRequiredFiles: Relative file paths that must exist after installation (e.g., 7DaysToDieServer.x86_64). If any file is missing, MSM stops launch with a clear error message.
reference.runtimeStopGracePeriodSeconds: Grace period in seconds (5..600) when stopping container before SIGKILL. Default: 30.
reference.runtimeStartupCheckSeconds: Delay in seconds (0..300) before first log check during startup (important for large Wine/Proton images). Default: 5.0.
reference.runtimeAllowUnprivilegedUserNamespaces: Allows nested unprivileged user namespaces for runtimes such as UMU/pressure-vessel. Default: false. Only Docker seccomp is relaxed; cap-drop=ALL, no-new-privileges, the non-root user, and the host-network/privileged bans remain active.
reference.runtimeSeedFiles: List of default files written only when missing (seed-once). Each entry: file + content. Port tokens allowed. Runs before configPatches.

howto.h1: How do I enable Steam Workshop?
howto.b1: Set supportsMods=true, supportsSteamWorkshop=true, and add the workshopAppId in the 'mods' object. Set modInjection to 'startupArg' or 'file', depending on how the game loads mods.
howto.hCurseForge: How do I enable CurseForge mods?
howto.bCurseForge: Set supportsMods=true, supportsCurseForge=true and add the curseforgeGameId (e.g. 83374 for ARK: Survival Ascended or 432 for Minecraft). For file-based games like Minecraft, set curseforgeInstallPath to 'mods' or 'plugins'. For games like ASA that load mods via startup parameters, set modInjection to 'startupArg' and modStartupArgumentSeparator to ','. The API key is stored globally in the panel under Settings → CurseForge.
howto.h2: How do I patch a configuration file?
howto.b2: Use 'runtime.configPatches'. Required fields per patch: type ('ini' or 'regex'), file (relative path), and value. For type=ini, section (INI section, e.g. 'URL') and key are also required. For type=regex, regex (search pattern as regular expression) is required instead. Port placeholders are allowed in value ({GAME_PORT} etc.) — but NOT {ENV.<KEY>} or {MOD_ARG}, as those are only valid in the startup command.
howto.hSeedFiles: How do I supply default configuration files (seedFiles)?
howto.bSeedFiles: Use 'runtime.seedFiles' (list of objects with 'file' and 'content'). MSM writes these files ONLY when missing from the server directory (seed-once). This allows delivering default configs without overwriting user changes. Combined with 'runtime.configPatches', both newly seeded and downloaded game files are automatically patched before every startup (e.g. adjusting ports or disabling buggy crossplay modules).
howto.h3: How do I host Discord bots or other apps from GitHub?
howto.b3: Use source.type=github (generic, not Discord-only): repo as owner/repo, branch (e.g. main), optional subPath for monorepos. checkBased pulls via git fetch/reset before start/restart. Optional setupCommands (argv lists, e.g. npm ci) after clone/pull. runtime.startupProfiles picks the start command (package.json → npm start, bot.py → python3 bot.py). Secrets (.env) are preserved by the config backup.
howto.b3_extra: MSM's automatic updater will preserve your configuration files: Typical config extensions like .json, .env, .toml, .yaml, .yml, .ini, .cfg, or .txt (under 2MB in size, outside of system/data directories) are backed up temporarily during updates/reinstalls and restored automatically.
howto.h4: How does MSM check game updates vs Workshop mods?
howto.b4: Workshop mods use the Steam API; outdated mods install on restart. Steam game binaries use buildid + branch. GitHub/HTTP sources compare remote vs local (commit or Last-Modified) and update on checkBased before start/restart. The update badge and “Check game updates” show for managed sources (steam, http, github) — workshop mods stay in the mod manager.
howto.h5: How do I limit backups to config and saves?
howto.b5: Add an optional top-level backup block with includePaths: relative paths or globs (e.g. ConanSandbox/Saved/Config, profiles). MSM archives only existing matches — recommended for large Steam games.

updates.body: Server binaries and Workshop mods are handled separately. Both can show status in the panel (mod status vs server update badge); installation happens during lifecycle (start/restart), not while the server is running.

troubleshooting.err1Body: While the panel removes // comments, syntax errors (like missing commas) will still cause the upload to fail. Use a JSON linter.
troubleshooting.err2Body: The command in runtime.startup cannot contain shell substitutions or control operators ($, backticks, $(), ${}, &&, ||). The panel tokenizes the command strictly as an array to prevent command injections.
troubleshooting.err3Body: All paths in ensureDirs, configPatches, mod lists, and extractTo must be relative to the server directory. Absolute paths (/etc) or escapes (../) are rejected.
troubleshooting.err4Title: Docker image unavailable / image or tag not found
troubleshooting.err4Body: Check runtime.image exactly, including the tag. ghcr.io/ptero-eggs/yolks:wine is a different tag than ghcr.io/ptero-eggs/yolks:wine_staging. Test as the msm user with docker pull <image> and DOCKER_HOST pointing to the rootless Docker socket.
troubleshooting.err5Title: failed to extract layer ... to overlayfs
troubleshooting.err5Body: Docker found the image but failed while extracting it. The usual cause is a full partition. Check DockerRootDir with docker info, then run df -h and df -ih for that path. Large Wine/game images should have at least 10-20 GB free.
troubleshooting.err6Title: Rootless Docker Daemon not running for user msm
troubleshooting.err6Body: The panel user's rootless Docker daemon is not running or its socket is not reachable. Check systemctl --user status docker as the msm user and verify that DOCKER_HOST points to unix:///run/user/<msm_uid>/docker.sock.
troubleshooting.err7Body: MSM blocks the start when Docker would bind to all interfaces. Set a concrete host IP in the server detail view. This protects firewall rules from being bypassed accidentally.
troubleshooting.err8Body: Some Steam servers or Workshop downloads require a global Steam login. Configure the account in Settings. Passwords are not shown in logs or toasts.
troubleshooting.err9Title: Hytale OAuth or downloader access failed
troubleshooting.err9Body: On the first Hytale start, the console shows an OAuth link. Open it, enter the code, and use a Hytale account with server-download access. If you see 403 or Unauthorized, the account usually lacks access, the code expired, or the local Hytale downloader credential file in that server directory must be renewed.
troubleshooting.err10Title: Permission repair / chmod: Operation not permitted on start
troubleshooting.err10Body: Often caused by root-owned files in the server directory (e.g. manual sync with sudo) while MSM uses rootless Docker. MSM no longer aborts start for this; check the console hint. Prefer MSM-driven copies or chown to the container UID (runtime.user).

exec.intro: The Exec tab lets authenticated users with the server.console.exec permission run one-shot commands inside the MSM-managed container of a server — e.g. docker compose logs, npm run build, ls -la /data. Self-hosted, but commands run ONLY inside the MSM container of that one server, never on the host or in other containers.
exec.safety1: argv instead of a shell string: we pass the command array 1:1 to docker exec. There is no shell in between, so shell metacharacters (;, |, $(), backticks) cannot be escalated — they are literal text.
exec.safety2: The container name comes only from container_name_for(server.id): there is no request field that lets the user influence the target container. Host exec or another server's container are structurally impossible.
exec.safety3: Blueprint gate: runtime.enableExec must be true, otherwise the endpoint returns 403 even for owners with the permission. Default is false.
exec.safety4: Separate server.console.exec permission (not console.write). Users get exec explicitly.
exec.safety5: Limits: 1..32 arguments, each max 4096 characters. Timeout 1..600 seconds from blueprint. Output capped at 256 KiB with a [truncated] marker.
exec.safety6: Audit log: server id, user id and argv are logged. Output (which may contain sensitive data) is NOT logged.

ai_chat_use.desc: Allows the AI chat. Role limits and tool permissions are checked in the backend on top of this.

ai_voice_use.title: Talk to the AI
ai_voice_use.desc: Allows voice mode. Kept separate from chat because changes are confirmed by voice here instead of by click — including deletion and restoring backups. Whoever holds this permission can trigger by voice anything they could trigger in chat: the permission check is the same, the confirmation is not. Voice also costs extra, one transcription per utterance and the voice per spoken character.

ai_attachments_use.title: Use AI attachments
ai_attachments_use.desc: Allows checked attachments in the AI chat; file type, size and path limits stay in force.

ai_memory_use.title: Use AI memory
ai_memory_use.desc: Allows your own AI memory, which stays visible and deletable.

ai_skills_use.title: Use AI skills

ai_skills_manage.title: Manage AI skills

ai_web_search_use.title: Use AI web search
ai_web_search_use.desc: Allows the AI to look things up on the web. It searches through the search service configured in the AI settings; without a key the tool is not offered at all. Results are truncated and treated as untrusted data.

ai_autonomous_use.title: Use autonomous AI mode
ai_autonomous_use.desc: Allows the user to enable autonomous mode per server or panel-wide. Without that extra approval every action still needs confirmation; permissions apply unchanged.

ai_tasks_manage.title: Manage recurring AI tasks
ai_tasks_manage.desc: Allows creating standing orders — in the chat or by hand in the task list on the AI page; without this permission there is neither a button nor a list there. A due order runs in the background without the user present, but with that user's permissions and from that user's quota. Orders that change something also require autonomous mode.

ai_background_use.title: Use AI workers in the background
ai_background_use.desc: Allows the AI to hand orders to workers that keep working in the background — even while the conversation continues or the browser is closed. A worker runs with the permissions and from the quota of the user who gave the order; every change to servers still requires confirmation, exactly as in the chat. Without this permission the AI works in a single run, as before.

ai_desktop_use.title: AI tools on your own computer
ai_desktop_use.desc: Allows the AI to work on the user's computer — through the Smart System app, never through the panel. It may look at whatever the user can see: drives, folders, disk space, the screen and a virus check — all read-only, and an indicator lights up at the edge of the screen whenever it looks. Creating and changing files happens only inside the self-chosen sandbox folder. Cleaning up is also allowed outside it: deleted items go to the recycle bin, permanently only on explicit request, and with autonomous mode off a card with the full list appears first. Windows itself, program folders and other user profiles stay locked until the user unlocks them in the app's settings. It takes over mouse and keyboard without asking only in autonomous mode; with that off, the user must confirm it on their machine, and the grant is then time-limited and revocable at any time. A request from the browser never reaches these tools — the origin is in the token of the paired session, no client can claim it.

ai_desktop_install.title: Install desktop artifacts & software
ai_desktop_install.desc: Allows the AI to download, test (Defender & Sandbox), deploy with snapshot rollback, or start user-level installers for software, game mods, and applications via the Smart System app.

ai_mailbox_use.title: Use AI Mailbox Integration
ai_mailbox_use.desc: Allows the AI to search linked user mailboxes, read emails, and draft messages. Sending emails always requires explicit user confirmation.

ai_calendar_use.title: Use AI Calendar Integration
ai_calendar_use.desc: Allows the AI to query linked user CalDAV calendars and prepare events. Creating or deleting events always requires explicit user confirmation.

ai_usage_read_all.title: View overall AI usage
ai_usage_read_all.desc: Shows under Settings → AI which user spent how many tokens and how much money. This makes other users' behaviour visible — which is why it is a permission of its own and not part of the settings permission. Everyone sees their own usage without it.

panel.title: Panel / control plane
panel.description: Backend, DIS sidecar, panel PostgreSQL, frontend, local agent and installation scripts. This is the central control plane.

frontend.title: Standalone frontend
frontend.description: The already-built static Vite bundle plus the public environment example. No backend or agent sources are included.

node.title: Remote node

install.title: Recommended one-command panel installation
install.description: Point an HTTPS domain at the fresh Ubuntu or Debian host, then run the public bootstrap as root. Replace panel.example.com with your real panel domain.
install.releaseNote: The bootstrap prefers the tested msm-panel artifact from the latest GitHub release. install.sh remains the central installer for bootstrap, simple and interactive modes: on minimal systems it installs every required base package and safely repairs an incomplete Caddy repository without replacing an existing Caddyfile.

topology.title: Example topology: 20 hosts
topology.control: Host 1 runs the panel/control plane and can also serve the frontend. It coordinates users, configuration and the remote nodes.
topology.nodes: Hosts 2 through 20 each run only the remote agent. None of these nineteen nodes needs a repository checkout.
topology.split: Optional split layout: host 1 serves the static frontend, host 2 runs the control plane, and hosts 3 through 20 are remote nodes.

migration.title: Safely split an existing installation
migration.description: Run the assistant on the existing all-in-one installation. It collects your choices and migrates game servers before the final backend cutover so that only one control plane is authoritative.

1.title: Connect an external frontend
1.description: Checks the already-built HTTPS frontend, separates panel and API origins, and verifies CORS, cookies and the API-only Caddy site.

2.title: Move game servers
2.description: Copies selected stopped servers with saves, mods, workshop files, backups and assigned PostgreSQL databases. Source data is retained.

3.title: Move the backend
3.description: Pre-installs the fresh target, automatically uses the owner-confirmed node ID, then transfers the panel database, configuration, DIS secrets, panel backups and community blueprints during the short cutover.

migration.externalBoundary: MSM cannot change the DNS A/AAAA record at an external provider or grant the one-time owner approval for a new agent. These boundaries are shown clearly and never bypassed.
migration.rollback: Before target commit, a failure restarts the old control plane. After successful target verification it stays disabled to prevent split brain. The assistant keeps source data and the old control plane as a rollback basis and never deletes them automatically.

enrollment.title: Connect a new node

1.title: Open Nodes
1.description: Sign in as owner, open Nodes and choose Add node.

2.title: Copy the command
2.description: The panel displays a public, secret-free installation command.

3.title: Run it once
3.description: Execute the command as root on the new Ubuntu or Debian node.

4.title: Create identity locally
4.description: The installer creates the agent token and TLS certificate on the node, then sends token and fingerprint to the panel over HTTPS. The token is stored DIS-encrypted and never shown in the UI, URL or logs.

5.title: Compare the code
5.description: The pending enrollment appears in the panel. Compare the short displayed code before approving it.

6.title: Approve and verify
6.description: Owner approval gates the panel's reachability, agent-token and TLS-pin checks. Only a successful verification activates the node.

enrollment.fallback: Pending enrollments expire after 15 minutes and are rate-limited. Manual host, token and fingerprint entry remains available only as a fallback for agents installed separately or connected through a special network setup.

guardian.title: Persistent Guardian state
guardian.intro: Node-local Guardian operational state is persistent operational data, not a cache. It must not be served by the web server or mounted into game-server containers.

path.title: Default path
path.body: /var/lib/msm-agent/guardian; systemd creates the parent through StateDirectory=msm-agent and assigns it to the agent service.

environment.title: Environment
environment.body: MSM_GUARDIAN_STATE_DIR deliberately changes the path. MSM_GUARDIAN_LOOP_INTERVAL_SECONDS controls reconciliation, default 5.0 seconds; lower values increase Docker and I/O load.

contents.title: Contents and limits
contents.body: It contains accepted and observed states, unconfirmed incidents, and at most ten recovery lock-file backups per server. Individual files are limited to 1 MiB and use mode 0600.

backup.title: Backup
backup.body: Before node reinstall or migration, back up the Guardian path together with server data. Installers and updates preserve this path.

restore.title: Restore
restore.body: Stop the agent, restore the path with unchanged ownership and restrictive permissions, then start the agent and verify heartbeat, state, generation, and hash in the panel.

migration.title: Migration and split brain
migration.body: An old state copy must never be active on two nodes at once. Recovery backups live below recovery-backups/<server-id>/<backup-id>/.

descriptions.panel: Installable control plane with backend, DIS, frontend, agent package and installation scripts.
descriptions.frontend: Only the built frontend/dist directory and the public environment example.
descriptions.agent: Agent sources and installer for controlled offline or automation scenarios.
descriptions.sums: SHA-256 checksums for verifying all three archives before installation.

smartSystem.title: MSS — Maunting Smart System (desktop app)
smartSystem.intro: Optional Desktop App for Windows: the same ongoing chat as in the browser, a wake word trained offline, and work inside a folder the user picks. The app does not replace the panel — it is a second way into the same conversation, with the same permissions and a computer attached.

artifact.title: Installer
artifact.body: The smart-system-release.yml workflow builds the NSIS installer on smart-v* tags, deliberately separate from the panel releases. Windows only: audio ducking, takeover and the credential vault are Windows features.

oberflaeche.title: One interface
oberflaeche.body: The app renders the same AI page as the browser — chat, realtime mode, guardian window, task list, reasoning picker — built from the same frontend code (npm run build:desktop). There is no second chat implementation that could go stale; the only difference is the transport: bearer tokens instead of cookies, including on the voice WebSocket. If the voice handshake fails, the app asks the backend about its capabilities and, on an older deployment, reports “The panel is too old for the app’s voice mode” — the fix is a panel update.

permission.title: Permissions
permission.body: Pairing and chatting needs ai.chat.use. Tools on the user's own computer additionally need ai.desktop.use; without it the app fetches no jobs, and the AI is not even offered those tools. From the browser it never gets them — nobody is sitting in front of the confirmation card there.

sandbox.title: Sandbox
sandbox.body: The AI works exclusively inside a folder the user selects. The resolved path is checked, not the requested one — a link pointing outward does not lead out either. Deleted files go to the recycle bin.

takeover.title: Mouse and keyboard
takeover.body: With autonomous mode off, the AI can only ask to take over; only the human at the machine can grant it, on a confirmation card and for a limited time. The deadline lives in the app, not in the panel, and can be ended at any moment. In autonomous mode the card is skipped — the operator decided in advance, just as for every other action.

pairing.title: Signing in by pairing
pairing.body: The app knows neither password nor 2FA code. In the panel under Profile → AI a code is created (ten minutes, exactly once) and entered in the app; only its hash is stored. This is necessary because a captcha widget cannot work inside a Tauri window — password, 2FA and captcha therefore stay entirely in the browser. Paired devices can be locked out individually from the same place.

uninstall.title: Uninstalling
uninstall.body: In the app under Settings → Danger zone. It also removes what Windows leaves behind: settings, voice recordings, the credential entry and autostart. The sandbox folder stays — it belongs to the user.

smartSystem.unsigned: The installer is not signed. Windows SmartScreen reports an unknown publisher; it can be started via “More info”. Compare the SHA256 sum from the release first — it replaces the missing signature.

compatibility.title: PostgreSQL only for new installations
compatibility.description: PostgreSQL is the only supported panel runtime database. SQLite code exists solely for a one-time, verified migration of legacy installations. A first install interrupted after role and database creation can be validated and continued without deletion using --resume-partial; foreign PostgreSQL state remains blocked.

hoster.title: Hoster and shop integration (optional)
hoster.intro: An external shop can order, suspend and terminate servers automatically. MSM only handles the technical access and the server — not the shop, the payment or the invoice.

setup.title: Setup
setup.body: Settings → Hoster tab. First create a service user holding the 'servers.create' permission, then the integration. The API key is shown exactly once and stored only as a hash.

api.title: External API
api.body: The shop reports only the desired state via PUT /api/hoster/v1/services/{id}. Authentication uses the X-MSM-Hoster-Key header; a repeated call never creates a second server.

lifecycle.title: Lifecycle
lifecycle.body: active, suspended and terminated. Suspension stops the server and revokes customer permissions but keeps the panel account. Termination sets a grace period and deletes nothing immediately.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.body: Status notifications are signed with HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp and body; the secret is never transmitted. Deliveries are persisted and survive a panel restart.

handoff.title: One-click handoff
handoff.body: The shop creates a link valid for five minutes and exactly one use that can only lead to allowed panel pages. Only its hash is stored.

selfHosted.title: Self-hosted stays untouched
selfHosted.body: Without a configured integration nothing changes: no extra service, no open endpoint and no new mandatory fields.

credentials.title: Credentials and Kubernetes
credentials.intro: GitHub tokens and Steam accounts can exist panel-wide, per user or per server. Nothing changes for self-hosted operation: without an own assignment the panel-wide access still applies.

order.title: Resolution order
order.body: Server assignment before environment variable before panel access. The assignment comes first because it is the most specific statement.

vault.title: Personal vault
vault.body: Profile → Credentials. The value is stored encrypted and never shown again — only the name, username and last four characters remain visible.

server.title: Server assignment
server.body: The section in the server detail appears only if that server's blueprint requires credentials. You may only assign entries you own.

fallback.title: Central fallback
fallback.body: Settings → Hoster. Switched off, no server silently runs with the operator's credentials; it reports a comprehensible error instead.

limits.title: Deliberate limits
limits.body: The Steam Web API key stays panel-wide. A bound credential cannot be deleted while a server uses it, and an undecryptable one never falls back to the panel silently.

kubernetes.title: Kubernetes
kubernetes.body: The manifests under deploy/kubernetes run the control plane. Game servers remain Docker containers on the connected nodes. Exactly one panel replica, and the DIS sidecar runs in the same pod. The AI run broker and AI report office are process-local too: reports from background tasks live in the database and survive a restart, only live-following breaks off briefly.

voice.title: Voice mode
voice.intro: Talk to the AI instead of typing — with the very same agent: same conversation, same run, same tools, same permissions. It is not a second model but the ordinary chat run with a converter in front and behind. Switch at the top right of the AI page: the chat gives way to an orb that moves with the spoken word.

access.title: What has to be configured
access.body: Two things. On a chat access — OpenRouter or OpenAI — a “model for speech”. And a second access of type “ElevenLabs (Voice)” with key, speech model and voice ID. If either is missing, the switch does not appear at all. And the reverse proxy must allow the panel to use the microphone: the Caddy site from install.sh sets Permissions-Policy microphone=(self) — installations from before 2026-08-22 still carry microphone=(), which makes the browser block getUserMedia without ever asking. Edit the line by hand and reload Caddy.

model.title: Models and voice
model.body: Hearing: a transcription model such as openai/gpt-transcribe, called through /audio/transcriptions. It does not appear in the model dropdown — that reads /models, which lists chat models. Hence the text field. One trap on OpenRouter: that endpoint is paid from credits, not through your stored bring-your-own key — without credits the access keeps chatting but stops hearing. MSM_AI_STT_WEG=chat helps then: the audio goes as input_audio to a hearing-capable chat model, and free ones exist. Voice: eleven_flash_v2_5, about 75 ms of inference. The voice ID comes from your voice library and is a text field too — MSM does not know your voices and will not guess one.

permission.title: Permission ai.voice.use
permission.body: Separate from ai.chat.use because confirmation happens by voice rather than by click. The AI inherits exactly the speaker's permissions and nothing more — through their role or as a directly assigned user of a server. Without both accesses the switch does not appear at all, not greyed out.

confirm.title: Confirming by voice
confirm.body: The AI says what it intends to do; next to it a box names the action — with no button, because the decision is spoken. Out loud, “I’ll delete the server then” is clear enough to agree to and too vague to tell you which one. A clear “yes” executes. Clear means literally: the utterance must be nothing but consent — “yes, but check the logs first” is a new instruction, not consent. The spoken yes replaces the click and not a single check.

quota.title: Quota
quota.body: Every utterance is one request — the same booking as a typed message. A role limit of five requests per minute will therefore tear a conversation apart; with no limit set, nothing happens. In exchange, token and cost limits now apply exactly as they do in chat. MSM does not count ElevenLabs characters; a single answer is capped at 4,000. MSM does not count the transcription either: it precedes the run and belongs to none. The provider still bills it.

relay.title: Audio travels through the panel
relay.body: Browser → panel → provider, not around it. With a direct connection the tool loop would run through the browser — it would see every call and could invent some. The backend also decides when someone has stopped speaking. The keys never leave the panel process. No extra port; the reverse proxy must pass WebSocket upgrades under /api/, which it already does for the server console.

voice.spokenLimit: Deleting and restoring a backup can be confirmed by voice as well since 2026-08-16 — the operator decided this explicitly. The residual risk: the audit then records a spoken confirmation, and anyone listening in the room can utter it. If that goes too far, remove ai.voice.use from the role. Speech goes to the chat provider as audio and the answer text to ElevenLabs; their EU data residency is reserved for enterprise customers.

docsOAuth.title: OAuth & Social Login
docsOAuth.subtitle: Wire up external identity providers for sign-in.

intro.body: OAuth / OIDC enables sign-in with external identity providers (IdP). The MSM backend alone decides whether a user is registered, linked, or only needs 2FA approval. The frontend only shows the available providers and starts the flow.

presets.title: Preset overview
presets.google: OpenID Connect, email and profile. Requires an OAuth client in Google Cloud Console.
presets.discord: OAuth 2.0, email + username. Requires an application in the Discord Developer Portal.
presets.github: OAuth 2.0, primary email + username. Requires an OAuth app in GitHub Settings → Developer settings.
presets.microsoft: OpenID Connect (multi-tenant), email + username. Requires an app registration in Microsoft Entra ID.
presets.twitter: OAuth 2.0 with PKCE, user ID and username. Requires an app in the Twitter Developer Portal.
presets.custom_oidc: Generic OIDC client: only the issuer is required, endpoints are discovered via /.well-known/openid-configuration. Suitable for Authentik, Keycloak, Zitadel, Auth0, Okta.
presets.custom_oauth2: Generic OAuth 2.0 client: endpoints must be set manually. For providers that do not fully implement OIDC.

create.title: Create a provider
create.step3: Pick a preset, choose a slug and a display name.
create.step4: Register an OAuth app / client in the IdP. Use EXACTLY the callback URL shown in the MSM as the redirect URI.
create.step5: Copy the client ID and client secret into the MSM form. The secret is stored Fernet-encrypted and is always masked in the UI.
create.step6: Enable the provider. The test button checks the configuration for consistency (slug, endpoints, preset).

security.title: Security & data minimisation
security.rule1: OAuth delivers identity only. Permissions are granted exclusively by the MSM backend.
security.rule2: Client secrets are never sent to the frontend in cleartext. The UI shows only a mask (****1234).
security.rule3: PKCE (S256) is enabled for all providers — prevents authorization code interception.
security.rule4: The state cookie is HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite=Lax, valid for 10 minutes and Fernet-encrypted.
security.rule5: If a user has 2FA enabled, the OAuth login is paused with a 5-minute challenge. The user must explicitly confirm the 2FA code.
security.rule6: Email verification is enforced by default: users with an unverified IdP email are rejected (toggle in the UI).
security.rule7: Auto-registration is OFF by default: only known users can sign in. Can be enabled globally in the UI.
security.rule8: Account linking is OFF by default: users cannot link OAuth providers to their password account on their own. Admins can enable it globally.

troubleshooting.err1Body: The redirect URI registered in the IdP must EXACTLY match the one shown in the MSM (including https vs http, path, query string).
troubleshooting.err2Body: The state cookie is valid for 10 minutes. Longer pauses require a fresh sign-in.
troubleshooting.err3Title: IdP does not return an email
troubleshooting.err3Body: Some providers (e.g. Twitter) only return the email if the user explicitly grants it. MSM rejects users without an email when "Require verified email" is on.
troubleshooting.err4Body: The provider is disabled or deleted in MSM. Enable it or re-create it.
troubleshooting.err5Body: The issuer must be a valid URL exposing /.well-known/openid-configuration. On air-gapped systems, use Custom OAuth 2.0 with manual endpoints.

oauth_provider_unavailable: This login provider is not available.
oauth_idp_error: The identity provider rejected the sign-in.
oauth_invalid_callback: Response from the identity provider was incomplete.
oauth_state_mismatch: Security token mismatch. Please sign in again.
oauth_exchange_failed: Code exchange at the identity provider failed.
oauth_profile_fetch_failed: Could not load the profile from the identity provider.
oauth_profile_invalid: Response from the identity provider was invalid.
oauth_preset_unknown: Preset for this provider is unknown.
oauth_forbidden: Sign-in with this provider is not allowed for your account.
oauth_registration_failed: Auto-registration failed. Please contact an admin.
no_matching_user: No MSM account exists for this identity yet. Please register locally first and then link the provider in your profile, or enable auto-registration in the OAuth settings.
oauth_link_invalid: This request has expired or is invalid.

webhook.label: Label (optional)
webhook.targetUrlHelp: You receive this URL from the receiving system (bot provider, monitor setup, etc.).
webhook.rotateMsg: The new secret is shown once. You must update it in the receiver (bot, monitor) — otherwise it will stop receiving events.
webhook.disableMsg: Incoming events will no longer be sent. The event history is preserved.
webhook.deleteMsg: The subscription will be removed. Events will no longer be sent to this URL.

panelBackups.title: Panel Backups
panelBackups.subtitle: Backups of the MSM panel (database + configuration)
panelBackups.confirmDelete: Really delete this panel backup? This action cannot be undone.
panelBackups.retentionHint: The oldest backups are automatically deleted when a new one is created.
panelBackups.restoreModalSubtitle: Run the script on the panel server as root.
panelBackups.restoreModalWarning: WARNING: This script stops the MSM panel service and overwrites the database and configuration files!

privacy.s3SectionBody: When the administrator configures S3-compatible storage, encrypted backups may be uploaded to external S3 storage operated by third parties. These backups are encrypted client-side (zero-knowledge): the S3 provider receives only encrypted data and cannot read the backup contents. The decryption password never leaves this MSM instance and is never transmitted to the S3 provider.
privacy.s3ItemEncryption: Encryption is performed client-side before upload (AES-256-GCM)
privacy.s3ItemZeroKnowledge: S3 provider can only view encrypted data (zero-knowledge)
privacy.s3ItemPassword: Decryption is only possible with the backup password set on this instance
privacy.s3ItemLocalOnly: No configuration: backups remain local — no data is transmitted to third parties
privacy.section4Updated: No personal data is shared with third parties. For technical reasons, encrypted backup data may be stored on external S3-compatible storage if the administrator configures it (see section 6). In that case, the storage provider receives only encrypted data.

privacyNotice.title: Understand how this instance handles data
privacyNotice.description: MSM uses necessary browser storage for sign-in, security, and preferences. If your operator enables a third-party support widget, it loads only after this notice is acknowledged and may process connection and message data under the operator’s policy.

privacyPolicy.title: Privacy policy
privacyPolicy.intro: In a time of increasing digital surveillance and dwindling privacy, Maunting Studios stands for the counter-model: protection requires trust. This policy describes transparently and comprehensively all data flows of the Maunting Service Manager and the Desktop App. We never track or surveil anyone covertly: all actions are transparent, auditable, self-hosted, and remain under the complete control of the user.
privacyPolicy.callout: Summary: Maunting Studios – Protection requires trust. Complete data sovereignty, no covert tracking: High-risk capabilities (like Computer-Use) are disabled by default, and every AI action remains transparently controllable and switchable.

scope.heading: 1. Scope and operator
scope.body: MSM is self-hosted. Maunting Studios provides the software; the organization operating this instance determines purposes, optional integrations, access rules, and retention for its deployment.

accounts.heading: 2. Accounts, authentication, and authorization
accounts.body: The panel processes the account and security data needed to authenticate users, enforce permissions, and investigate security-relevant activity.

items.identity: Username and email address for account identification and sign-in
items.security: Password verification data, sessions, optional two-factor authentication data, and recovery state
items.rbac: Roles, global permissions, server-specific permissions, and ownership status
items.audit: Security and audit events such as sign-ins, permission changes, and administrative actions

infrastructure.heading: 3. Server and node data
infrastructure.body: Operating infrastructure requires metadata. It is available only to authorized users and is not described as anonymous or metadata-free.

items.server: Server names, game types, resource limits, network bindings, ports, status, configuration, and backup metadata
items.node: Node names, host addresses, pinned TLS fingerprints, versions, health status, capacity, and utilization metrics
items.operations: Administrative operation results, logs, and command output may contain infrastructure or user-provided data

protection.heading: 4. Credentials and backups
protection.body: MSM separates secrets from ordinary metadata and protects them at the component that needs them.

items.dis: Sensitive panel credentials, including agent and provider credentials, are encrypted through DIS before database storage
items.backups: Backup archives are encrypted by the responsible agent before transfer to configured remote storage
items.metadata: Operational metadata needed to select, restore, and audit backups remains visible to the authorized instance and configured storage provider

providers.heading: 5. Optional external providers
providers.body: No optional provider is required by the base panel. When the operator enables one, the provider receives the data needed for that integration.

items.email: Email delivery provider: recipient address and message delivery data
items.captcha: CAPTCHA provider: browser, network, and challenge data according to that provider’s policy
items.oauth: OAuth provider: account identifier, profile data released by the provider, and authentication metadata
items.support: Support-widget provider: connection metadata and content users submit to the widget; the widget is held until this notice is acknowledged
items.s3: S3-compatible provider: encrypted backup objects plus technical object, account, timing, and transfer metadata

ai.heading: 6. AI assistant and external model providers
ai.body: AI features are optional. When used, the panel processes the conversation and sends the message with minimized, redacted context to the selected model provider. The operator determines available providers and must document their terms and lawful basis.

items.messages: Global and server-specific chat histories are linked to the account, stored in the panel, and can be deleted by the user
items.context: The submitted message, limited prior messages, and approved server metadata are transferred; IP addresses, installation paths, complete configurations, and detected secrets are excluded from model context
items.credentials: Personal and central provider API keys are context-bound and encrypted through DIS, then shown only as configuration status or a mask
items.usage: Provider, model, token reservation, actual or conservatively estimated usage, and timestamps are stored to enforce quotas; monetary cost is not claimed without an authoritative price source
items.memory: Optional memory entries are stored encrypted and cryptographically bound to their scope, and can be reviewed and deleted at any time. There are five scopes: personal entries and personal server-scoped notes are visible to nobody but the user; team entries are visible to every member of that team; a server's own knowledge is visible to everyone allowed to see that server and remains when its author leaves the panel; panel-wide entries are visible to every user of the panel
items.memoryConsent: Personal memory is disabled by default and only becomes active after explicit consent in the chat; consent can be withdrawn at any time and also covers your own server-scoped notes. Shared scopes (team, server, panel-wide) do not depend on that consent but on permissions – they hold operational knowledge, not personal data. Encryption protects the database at rest; the plaintext of remembered entries is transmitted to the chosen model provider with every request
items.attachments: Approved text, configuration, log, and image attachments are size- and type-checked, stored encrypted in the panel, and transferred with the conversation to the selected model provider
items.autonomy: Autonomous mode is optional and must be granted explicitly, per server or panel-wide; granted actions run without a further prompt but are still checked against the user's permissions unchanged and are recorded in full in the audit log as executed automatically
items.tools: When tools are used, limited and redacted excerpts from server logs, configuration files, mod and backup lists and Guardian incidents may be transmitted to the model provider; these results are stored for follow-up questions in the same chat and are deleted together with the chat
items.guardian: With autonomy granted, a Guardian incident can trigger processing while the user is not present: the incident type, its status and the server data already shared with the assistant are transmitted; log excerpts are additionally stripped of public IP addresses and email addresses. Usage and responsibility remain with the grantor. The result report sent by email contains model-generated text.
items.tasks: A standing task created in chat or in the task list (“AI task”) stores its name, instruction, schedule, time zone and delivery channel, and triggers processing at the agreed time while the user is not present. It runs in the background with the permissions and quota of whoever created it; on each due run the instruction and the server data it retrieves are transmitted to the selected model provider. On request the result is additionally sent by email to the stored address and contains model-generated text. Tasks can be listed, paused and deleted from the chat and the task list at any time.
items.mailboxes: Linked email mailboxes (IMAP / SMTP): Stored credentials (passwords, app passwords, or OAuth tokens) are encrypted with DIS AES-256-GCM and never leave the panel in plaintext. Emails are searched or read solely upon your explicit instruction. The AI assistant never sends emails autonomously: every email transmission is presented in the chat as an action proposal card with subject, recipient, and content, and is only sent after your explicit confirmation.
items.calendars: Integrated & linked calendar: Events of the native calendar remain within the local panel database under full user data sovereignty. For external CalDAV accounts, credentials are encrypted with DIS AES-256-GCM. The AI only reads events upon specific request. Creating, modifying, or deleting events produces an action proposal card in the chat and is executed only after user confirmation (or logged automatically when autonomous mode is enabled).

desktopApp.heading: 7. The desktop app (Maunting Smart System)
desktopApp.body: The Maunting Smart System is an optional Windows app that runs on the user’s computer and works there on behalf of the AI. It is not a second panel but the same account with a computer attached: pairing happens through a code issued by the panel, and without the “AI tools on your own computer” permission it fetches no jobs at all. This section describes what stays on the machine and what leaves it. All outgoing connections go exclusively to the panel address entered during setup: there is no updater, no telemetry and no hard-wired third party.

items.computerUse: Computer-Use & Desktop Control (disabled by default): Computer-Use is completely deactivated upon installation. Only after your explicit activation in the settings and confirmation of the educational dialog can the AI control mouse and keyboard or inspect the screen. With autonomous mode disabled, every single action requires manual on-screen confirmation.
items.wakeword: Wake word (off by default): once enabled, the app continuously reads the microphone and compares what it hears against a reference model, entirely on the machine with no network connection. Until the word is recognised, not a single audio sample leaves the process, and nothing is recorded. Continuous listening creates a measurable CPU load (roughly one sixth of a core).
items.wakewordAufnahmen: Calibration voice recordings: to train the model you speak your chosen name several times. These are real voice recordings and are kept indefinitely as WAV files in the local app data directory, together with the reference model derived from them. They are never transmitted. They are removed by “Reset” in the wake word settings or by uninstalling.
items.sprachsitzung: Voice session: only after the wake word is recognised (or after the voice shortcut is pressed) does the app open the audio channel to the panel and transmit your utterance. The panel forwards it to the configured model provider for transcription; the spoken reply is additionally produced by a speech provider. From that point the statements in section 6 about external model providers apply.
items.bildschirm: Screenshots: the AI can look at the main screen. The image is downscaled, never written to disk, and transmitted as a tool result to the panel, which stores it encrypted and passes it to the model provider. The provider therefore sees everything visible at that moment, including other windows, messages and open documents. An indicator lights up at the edge of the screen for every capture; it cannot be switched off.
items.dateien: Read access to the computer: the AI can inspect drives, folders and disk space, as far as the signed-in Windows user may do so. Drive details as well as folder and file names with sizes are transmitted. File contents are only read and transmitted from the sandbox folder you select yourself. Whether the Windows system area may be read is configured per account in the panel.
items.schreiben: Write access: creating and changing files happens exclusively inside the sandbox folder you select. The resolved path is checked so that a link cannot lead out of the folder.
items.aufraeumen: Cleaning up outside the sandbox: deleting is possible outside it too. Deleted items go to the recycle bin; permanent deletion only on explicit request. Windows itself, program folders and other user profiles stay locked until you unlock them. The affected file paths, their size and their classification are sent to the panel and the model provider. With autonomous mode off, the app shows you the full list for confirmation first.
items.virenscan: Virus check: on request the app checks a file with the locally installed Microsoft Defender, without changing or removing it. The checked path and, if something is found, an excerpt of the Defender output (which contains file paths and threat names) go to the model provider.
items.eingabe: Mouse and keyboard: the app does not record your input. There is no capture of keystrokes or mouse movement, neither locally nor transmitted. Conversely the AI can take over mouse and keyboard; with autonomous mode off, every takeover must be confirmed on your machine and is time-limited. Text the AI types originates from the model and is contained in the transmitted job.
items.discordRpc: Discord Rich Presence (RPC): If the Discord desktop app is running on your computer, the desktop app can report your activity status locally via a Windows pipe to Discord (e.g. 'MSS Desktop Companion'). No server addresses, chat histories, IP addresses, or sensitive credentials are ever transmitted. This feature can be completely disabled in the desktop app configuration ('konfig.json' -> 'discord_rpc_aktiv': false).
items.lokal: What is stored locally: a plain-text configuration file (panel address, sandbox path, chosen assistant name, shortcuts, audio device names, wake word sensitivity), the wake word recordings and model, and exactly one entry in the Windows Credential Manager: the operating-system-encrypted refresh token of the paired session. Your password and two-factor code never reach the app; signing in works solely through the pairing code from the panel. Uninstalling removes all of it.

storage.heading: 8. Cookies and local browser storage
storage.body: The panel uses browser storage needed for secure operation and selected preferences.

items.session: Session or authentication cookies used to keep users signed in
items.csrf: CSRF protection values used to protect state-changing requests
items.preferences: Language and privacy-notice acknowledgement stored locally in the browser

retention.heading: 9. Retention and account deletion
retention.body: Retention depends on the operator’s configuration, infrastructure, backups, and legal obligations.

items.operator: The operator must define and document suitable retention periods and delete data that is no longer needed
items.deletion: Account deletion removes account-linked personal data from the active panel according to the implemented deletion flow; copies may remain temporarily in protected backups
items.audit: Security audit events may be retained in anonymized form so attacks and privileged changes remain traceable without retaining the deleted account identity

docsHosterApi.title: Hoster API
docsHosterApi.subtitle: Endpoint, webhook and signature reference for connecting an external shop.
docsHosterApi.optionalNote: Nothing in this document exists until an integration is created. A self-hosted setup without a shop has no endpoint that does anything without an API key.

principle.title: Core principle
principle.desiredState: The shop does not send commands, it sends a desired state. Instead of “start the server” it reports “this contract should be active”. That is the heart of idempotency: a command that arrives twice after a timeout is dangerous — a desired state that arrives twice is a no-op.
principle.noInternals: The shop deliberately sends no internal MSM details: no node ID, no port numbers, no install paths. It names a product key; MSM resolves blueprint, resources, host and ports itself.
principle.sharedLogic: Everything the hoster API triggers runs through the same services as a click in the panel. There is no path that bypasses permission checks, capacity checks, port allocation or Guardian.

auth.title: Authentication
auth.header: Every endpoint under /api/hoster/v1/ expects the integration API key in a header:
auth.noCookie: There is no cookie path. A browser session cannot reach these endpoints, and CORS is irrelevant for them — the call must be made server-side from the shop. Testing from the browser console will always fail; that is intentional, not a misconfiguration.
auth.hashOnly: MSM stores only the SHA-256 hash of the API key. The plaintext appears exactly once when it is created in the panel and cannot be retrieved afterwards. A missing and an invalid key return the same text and both a 401, so it is not detectable whether a key exists.
auth.boundary: The API key is equivalent to the rights of the integration's service user — no more. The security boundary is that user and their permissions, not the key.

endpoints.title: External API
endpoints.health: Verify the API key without changing anything.
endpoints.put: Set the desired contract state. Creates the contract on first call and continues it afterwards.
endpoints.get: Query the actual state. Returns 404 if the contract does not exist.
endpoints.handoff: Create a one-time link into the customer's panel.
endpoints.redeem: Redemption by the customer's browser. No API key — a human is clicking here.
endpoints.idempotencyKey: external_service_id is the contract identifier from the shop, at most 128 characters. Together with the integration it is unique and serves as the idempotency key.
endpoints.repeatable: The same call may be sent any number of times. A network retry does not create a second server: provisioning is bound to an idempotency key. Even two simultaneous first calls result in exactly one contract — the loser adopts the winner.
endpoints.async: Provisioning is asynchronous: after PUT the status may still be provisioning. The shop should either wait for the service.ready webhook or poll GET at intervals — not in a tight loop.

external_subject.body: Customer ID from the shop. The stable mapping uses this ID, not the email address — otherwise a customer changing their email would break the link.

product_key.body: Shop product key. MSM maps it to a blueprint and a resource package. On an existing contract a different value triggers a plan change.

email.body: Used only to create the panel user initially. MSM never takes over a shop password.

status_code.body: Stable error or hint code, otherwise null.

server_id.body: Internal server ID once one exists.

task_id.body: ID of the running provisioning or lifecycle operation.

correlation_id.body: Ties together all audit entries and webhooks of this contract.

terminate_after.body: ISO-8601 timestamp after which deletion happens following a cancellation.

updated_at.body: ISO-8601 timestamp of the last change.

states.title: State model
states.intro: desired_state is what the shop wants. status is what is. The two may temporarily diverge — that is exactly why there are two fields.
states.actualTitle: Actual states (set by MSM, each emits a webhook)
states.purge: The transition terminating → terminated does not happen in the API call but in a maintenance run that checks every minute whether terminate_after has been reached. The deletion path is the same as in the panel.
states.productChange: A plan change sets status_code to product_changed_manual_resize_required. The product mapping changes immediately; resource limits of a running server remain a deliberate operator action — they require a restart.
states.role: If the product mapping carries a role_id, the target state active grants that global role in addition to the customer's existing roles; suspended and terminated revoke it again — but only if no other active contract of the same customer still asks for that role, and never if it is a system role. Manually granted roles stay untouched. Global roles carry the AI quotas, among other things; that is exactly why the field exists: a larger plan brings more AI budget without anyone maintaining roles by hand.
states.roleRecord: What counts is the role a contract actually granted, not what its product carries right now. A tariff change therefore swaps the role instead of stacking it; if the operator changes or removes a product's role while contracts run on it, the originally granted role is still taken back; and a contract whose activation failed carries no role at all, even if its desired state remains active. If the operator deletes a product, the customer keeps the granted role until the contract ends.

desired.active: Contract is running. A server is created if needed and customer permissions are granted.
desired.suspended: Payment hold. The server is stopped and customer permissions are revoked. The panel account remains, data is preserved, and unsuspending later is possible.
desired.terminated: Cancellation. The server is stopped and a grace period is set. Nothing is deleted immediately.

status.pending: Contract created, technical work not yet started.
status.provisioning: The server is currently being created and installed.
status.ready: The server exists and is assigned to the customer.
status.suspended: Server stopped, customer permissions revoked, data preserved.
status.terminating: Cancelled, grace period running — the server still exists.
status.terminated: Grace period elapsed, server deleted. server_id is null afterwards.
status.failed: An operation failed. status_code names the reason.

errors.title: Errors and status codes
errors.persisted: A functional failure is not just an HTTP error. The contract remains queryable with status “failed” and a stable status_code, so the shop can find out afterwards what happened.
errors.roleEscalation: hoster_role_escalation fails hard on purpose instead of silently skipping the role: otherwise the customer would have a server without the quota they paid for, and nobody would notice.

http.200: Success. Also for PUT — there is no 201.
http.401: API key missing, invalid, or the integration is disabled.
http.422: Configuration error: unknown or disabled product, missing product key on creation, disabled service user, invalid handoff target.
http.503: Internal error while applying the change.

statusCode.port_conflict: No free port block on the target host.
statusCode.node_not_found: The product points at a node that does not exist.
statusCode.install_update_already_running: An installation is already running on the server.
statusCode.hoster_configuration_error: Product, service user or identity is not usable.
statusCode.hoster_role_escalation: The role configured on the product contains permissions the integration's service user does not hold itself. The contract is not carried out.
statusCode.hoster_internal_error: Unexpected error, traceable in the panel log.
statusCode.product_changed_manual_resize_required: A hint, not an error: plan changed, resources not yet adjusted.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.intro: MSM reports every state change to the HTTPS target configured in the panel — provided a webhook secret was created there. Without a target or secret nothing is queued, deliberately.
webhooks.bodyIntro: The body is the external API response schema without task_id, plus the event field:
webhooks.noInternals: Node names, host addresses, ports and install paths belong to the operator, not the shop — they intentionally do not appear.
webhooks.durable: Deliveries live in the database, not in memory: a panel restart during a backoff loses nothing. Permanently failed deliveries can be re-queued manually in the panel.
webhooks.payloadLimit: Payload limit 16 KiB. A larger body is silently dropped — no delivery is created and the receiver learns nothing about it. In normal operation this is unreachable, but a receiver should not rely on seeing every state change. The GET endpoint remains the authoritative source.
webhooks.clientError: A 200 is the acknowledgement. If the receiver answers with 4xx the delivery counts as permanently rejected — including 401. Verifying the signature incorrectly therefore loses events with no retry.

timeout.body: 10 seconds. After that MSM counts the attempt as failed — the actual processing belongs in a queue on the receiver side.

signature.title: Verifying the signature
signature.formula: The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over the string {timestamp}.{body}, emitted as sha256=<hex>. The timestamp is part of the signed data — without it an intercepted request could be replayed indefinitely.
signature.rawBody: Sign over the raw body, not over re-serialised JSON. MSM serialises without whitespace and with real non-ASCII characters. Parsing the body into an object and serialising it again almost certainly yields a different string and therefore a different signature. Most signature problems in practice have exactly this cause.
signature.exampleIntro: With these values every correct implementation must produce the same digest:

constantTime.body: hash_equals or hmac.compare_digest. A == on strings leaks the correct prefix through timing.

replay.body: MSM does not enforce one; ±5 minutes is recommended. The timestamp is signed and cannot be forged — but without a window an old, captured request stays reusable indefinitely.

idempotent.body: On a 5xx or timeout MSM retries. The same state report may arrive more than once; correlation_id plus status identifies it.

ordering.body: With retries an older report can arrive after a newer one. updated_at decides which is more recent.

fast.body: After 10 seconds MSM aborts and counts it as a failed attempt.

handoff.title: One-click handoff
handoff.intro: The customer clicks “Manage server” in the shop and lands signed in inside their MSM panel — with no second password and no separate registration.
handoff.serviceIdBody: The contract the link applies to.
handoff.targetBody: Target path in the panel. Only /servers, /servers/{id} and /dashboard are allowed. Default is /servers; anything else returns 422.
handoff.createOnClick: The link should therefore be created on click, not when the shop page is rendered.
handoff.splitHosting: Mind split hosting: the returned URL is built from MSM_PANEL_URL, while /api/hoster/handoff/{token} is a backend route. If frontend and API run on separate hosts, MSM_PANEL_URL must point at a host that forwards /api/* to the backend — otherwise the link goes nowhere.
handoff.oidc: The existing custom OIDC login can be used in addition. Both work at the same time: handoff for the direct click out of the shop, OIDC for a normal repeat login in the panel.

bound.body: To one specific user and contract

hashOnly.body: Hash only. The link appears neither in the audit log nor in logs.

concurrent.body: At most 5 tokens per user; older ones expire

uniformError.body: Unknown, expired and already used all lead uniformly to the login page. The response does not reveal which case applied.

admin.title: Panel administration
admin.intro: These endpoints serve the panel UI. They use cookie auth with CSRF protection, not the hoster API key. They are listed here in full for automation and infrastructure-as-code.
admin.create: Create an integration — the response contains the API key once
admin.update: Change name, status, service user, webhook target, grace period
