admin.simulate: Simulate a shop event (order, suspend, reactivate, terminate, webhook) in sandbox
admin.cleanSandbox: Clean all test data (contracts, servers, handoffs) of a sandbox integration
admin.productRole: The product body of PUT /integrations/{integration_id}/products also accepts role_id: the global role a customer receives in addition to their existing roles for as long as a contract runs on this product. Empty means no additional role. Two limits apply together: the caller may only assign roles whose permissions they hold themselves (otherwise 403; the admin system role stays reserved for the owner), and the integration's service user must hold them as well (otherwise 422). An integration can therefore never grant more than both together cover.
admin.openapi: The full OpenAPI schema is available at /api/docs and requires a login with the panel.settings.read permission.

serviceUser.term: The service user is the boundary
serviceUser.body: The integration can never do more than they can. They need servers.create and — for automatic deletion after the cancellation grace period — also servers.delete. The owner account is deliberately not allowed.

customerRights.body: Customers get permissions only on their own server, delegated per server instead of through a global role. Deliberately excluded: reinstall, network and resource management, container exec, database administration.

noDelete.body: A cascade would destroy the mapping between customers and their running servers while those servers keep running.

audit.body: Every operation appears with origin external and the shared correlation_id — without secrets and without customer identifiers in plaintext.

noSecrets.body: MSM stores no shop password and no payment data. It stores the external customer and contract identifier plus, optionally, the email used to create the panel user.

teams.title: Teams
teams.description: A team shares AI knowledge — skills and memories — and can bundle server permissions. Everyone has a personal one-person team so the assistant always has somewhere to learn.
teams.name: Team name
teams.myInvitationsHint: A team shares its AI knowledge and its server permissions with every member: whoever joins reads along — and whatever their assistant learns for the team, the others read. That is why only you decide whether you join.
teams.myUpgradesHint: You already belong to these teams — this is only about whether you may manage their shared knowledge from now on. If you accept, your assistant starts learning for that team, and whatever it stores there is readable by every member. If you decline, everything stays as it is.
teams.pendingInvitationsHint: Invited users are not members yet. The team's knowledge and server permissions reach them only once they accept — and only they can accept or decline.
teams.pendingUpgradesHint: These members are in the team already; only a management switch is being requested. You cannot raise it on your own — their consent flips it. Taking it back, however, is yours alone at any time.
teams.leaveConfirm: Leave “{{name}}”? The team's knowledge and server permissions will no longer reach you, and getting back in needs a new invitation.
teams.removeConfirm: Delete “{{name}}” along with all shared skills and memories?
teams.serversHint: Members receive the selected permissions on these servers. Only what you hold directly is offered — a team can never pass on more than its founder has. If you lose a permission, members lose it at the same moment.
teams.noAssignableServers: You currently hold no server permissions that could be passed on.
teams.knowledgeHint: What the assistant remembers for this team and which procedures it has learned here. Every member can read it; changing it needs the switches above.
teams.personalKnowledgeHint: Your personal AI knowledge. Nobody else sees it, regardless of permissions.
teams.personalMemoryElsewhere: Your personal memories are not here but in your profile — they are none of a team's business.
teams.noTeams: You are not a member of any team yet. A team shares skills, memories and server permissions with other users.

app.keinChatrecht: Your account lacks the permission to chat with the AI (ai.chat.use). Ask your operator to grant it — until then this window stays empty.

aufraeumen.warnungWeich: Everything goes to the recycle bin and can be restored from there.
aufraeumen.warnungGemischt: {{anzahl}} items marked “deleted at once” are caches and are removed directly — the recycle bin would not free any space there. Everything else can be restored from it.

systembereich.hinweis: How far Singra may reach into Windows itself – the Windows folder, program folders and other user profiles. Your own files are not affected by this.

erklaerung.aus: Singra neither looks nor touches anything there.
erklaerung.lesen: Singra may look – to find what is taking up space, for instance – but change nothing.
erklaerung.schreiben: Singra may also clean up there. With autonomous mode off it asks first; with it on, it does not.

wizard.adresseErklaerung: We need the address where the panel API answers. On a standard installation that is the same address you open in the browser. If the interface is hosted separately from the backend, it is the backend address — locally usually http://localhost:8000.
wizard.adresseHinweis: Not sure? Open the panel in a browser, F12 → Network, sign in — the host of the request to /api/auth/login is the right address.
wizard.adresseSchema: The address must start with https://. http:// is allowed for localhost only — the pairing code and the access tokens travel over this address, and without TLS anyone on the same network reads them.
wizard.antwortIstWebseite: This address serves the panel's interface, not its data. We need the address where the API answers — with split hosting that is the backend, locally usually http://localhost:8000.
wizard.kopplungErklaerung: Sign in to your panel in the browser and open Profile → AI → Pair devices. The code there is valid for ten minutes and exactly once.
wizard.codeHinweis: Case does not matter, and you can leave out the dashes.
wizard.geraetenameHinweis: Only for recognising it later, should you want to revoke its access.
wizard.personalisierungErklaerung: Give your assistant a name — that is how you address it and how it introduces itself. Both apply everywhere: here and in the panel.
wizard.agentnameHinweis: 2–32 characters; leave empty for the default name Singra.
wizard.sandboxErklaerung: The sandbox is the only folder where the AI may later create and edit files — for coding tasks, for example. It can also look at the rest of the computer (read-only, disk space for instance). It may clean up outside as well, but only by deleting, and into the recycle bin; creating and changing happens exclusively here.

uebernahme.erklaerung: Approval for {{minuten}} minutes. You can end it at any time, and it expires on its own afterwards. Mouse and keyboard remain yours — move the mouse and you notice immediately.

wakeword.keinMikrofon: No microphone found. Connect one or pick a default recording device in Windows — nothing can be recorded here until then.
wakeword.sprichJetzt: Recording {{nummer}} of {{gesamt}} — say the word now.
wakeword.kalibrierungFertig: All recordings are in. Now train.
wakeword.datenschutz: Everything stays on this computer: recordings and model live in the app data directory, no audio ever leaves the process.
wakeword.wortIstName: Your wake word is always your assistant’s name: “{{name}}”. Rename it in chat (“call yourself …”) or in the panel under Profile → AI.
wakeword.verfahrenAlt: This calibration comes from an older version of the app. Back then every recording was a fixed 2.5 seconds and therefore mostly room tone — detection only fired about three seconds after the word. Please record the name once more: reset, then the {{gesamt}} recordings. The sensitivity slider does not help here.
wakeword.neuKalibrieren: The model is still trained on “{{alt}}”, but your assistant is now called “{{neu}}”. Turn the wake word off, reset the calibration and record the new name — until then the app keeps listening for “{{alt}}”.
wakeword.aktivHinweis: On: say “{{name}}” and the overlay opens above everything. Off means off — the microphone is released and nothing turns listening back on by itself.
wakeword.lauschtNicht: The switch is on, but listening is not running — check the microphone and toggle it off and on again.
wakeword.schwelleHinweis: Low triggers more easily (including false hits), high demands a clearer match. Pause briefly after dragging — listening restarts with the new value.

gefahrenzone.erklaerung: Removes the app and everything it created on this computer: settings, your wake-word voice recordings, the entry in the credential manager and the autostart. Your sandbox folder stays.
gefahrenzone.sicherheitsfrage: Sure? The voice recordings and the stored sign-in will be deleted and cannot be recovered.
gefahrenzone.sandboxBleibt: Left untouched: your sandbox folder at {{pfad}}

computerUse.beschreibung: Allows the AI to control mouse and keyboard and inspect the screen. Disabled by default to protect your privacy.
computerUse.aktivierenWarnung: Important Security Notice: Enabling Computer-Use allows the AI to perform mouse movements, clicks, keystrokes, and screenshots on your machine after permission or in autonomous mode. With autonomous mode disabled, you must confirm each action manually in chat or via a confirmation dialog. Do you want to enable Computer-Use now?

artefakte.beschreibung: Allows the AI to download, test (Defender & Sandbox), deploy and roll back software, mods and installers.
artefakte.sandboxVerfuegbar: Ephemeral Windows Sandbox is available and active on this machine.
artefakte.sandboxNichtVerfuegbar: Windows Sandbox is not enabled or not supported (Hyper-V / BIOS Virtualization required).
artefakte.downloadLimitHinweis: Standard 10 GiB, configurable up to 100 GiB. Larger downloads are immediately aborted for security.
artefakte.suchwurzelnTitel: Approved search areas for games & software
artefakte.keineSuchwurzeln: No custom search folders added. Standard Steam libraries are detected automatically.
artefakte.aktivierenWarnung: Enabling this feature allows the AI to download files (such as game mods or software installers) on your request. All downloads undergo isolated quarantine, SHA-256 verification, Microsoft Defender scan and ephemeral Windows Sandbox testing prior to installation.

banner.computerUseHinweis: Computer-Use is currently disabled. The AI cannot control or inspect your desktop.

einstellungen.autostartHinweis: The app starts minimised to the tray — only then does the wake word listen from the start.
einstellungen.diagnoseHinweis: These buttons recolour the tray icon — and, while the overlay is open as a showcase, the voice orb too. When idle, the tray shows the logo.
einstellungen.fussnote: MSS — Maunting Smart System. Tray status and overlay run through the Rust backend.

hotkey.hinweis: Work everywhere, even with the window in the tray. Each shortcut can be disabled individually.

rechtliches.beschreibung: Full transparency, true data sovereignty, and no unnoticed actions on your systems.
rechtliches.datenschutzDesc: Learn in detail how your data, settings, and sessions are protected and minimally processed.
rechtliches.impressumDesc: Legal details and contact information of the operator of this server manager instance.
rechtliches.impressumKeinHinweis: No external operator imprint has been configured for this instance.

einstellungen.overlayTestenHinweis: Opens the overlay as a showcase: you see the orb and state text, but no microphone runs and nobody listens. Use the state buttons above to preview each colour. Click again (or X/ESC) to close.

schliessen.frage: Background means the window disappears while wake word and jobs keep running. Quit stops everything.

audio.hinweis: Which microphone listens and which speaker talks — independent of the Windows default. The choice applies to wake word and voice sessions and is saved.
audio.eingabeHinweis: If the chosen device is missing (unplugged), the app falls back to the Windows default until it returns — your choice is kept.
audio.ausgabeHinweis: The AI speaks through this device during voice sessions.
audio.duckingHinweis: While the AI speaks, the app lowers the volume of all other programs by 60% — music gets quieter instead of being drowned out. The test lowers it for three seconds: without music or video playing you will not hear anything.
audio.verarbeitungHinweis: Chromium's built-in, local processing — none of it leaves this machine. The defaults suit most microphones.
audio.echoHinweis: Filters the AI's own voice out of the microphone — without it, the AI hears itself and replies to itself (laptop without headphones).
audio.rauschenHinweis: Removes fans, hum and room noise from the signal.
audio.autogainHinweis: Levels quiet and loud voices automatically — helps weak microphones the most.
audio.verstaerkungHinweis: Raises or lowers the microphone signal in software. 100% means: do nothing — only touch it if the mic test sounds too quiet or clipped.
audio.testhoerenHinweis: Plays your own microphone through the chosen speaker — with exactly the processing above. Best with headphones: over speakers it will feed back.
audio.testhoerenFehler: Could not open the microphone — is it connected and allowed?

kalibrierung.frage: Your assistant is now called “{{neu}}” — the wake word is still calibrated to “{{alt}}”. You can record it again; until then the app keeps listening for “{{alt}}”. This is optional.
